chapter_name: Music, Percussion Instruments and their Classification
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the core elements of music and instrument classification! Explore the world of 'Avanaddha Vadya' (percussion/membrane instruments) and their significance.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Music (Sangeet) is the confluence of three arts: Vocal (Gayan), Instrumental (Vadan), and Dance (Nritya). Instruments provide essential support and rhythm to all three forms.

According to the ancient Indian text 'Natyashastra' (by Bharat Muni), musical instruments are classified into four categories: Tat (stringed), Sushir (wind), Ghan (solid/metallic), and Avanaddha (membrane/leather-covered).

These are instruments made of wood, clay, or metal, with their hollow mouths covered by animal skin (hide). Sound is produced by striking the skin with hands or sticks. Examples: Tabla, Pakhawaj, Dholak, Mridangam.
In Indian classical music, percussion instruments primarily maintain the Laya (Rhythm) and Taal (Beat cycle). Without them, any musical or dance performance feels incomplete and unstructured.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 Identify the Instrument
fun_activity.instructions: Look around your house or school. Stretch a rubber band and pluck it (acts like a 'Tat' vadya). Stretch a polythene sheet tightly over an empty box and tap it with your fingers (you just made an 'Avanaddha' vadya)!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the four types of instruments (Tat, Sushir, Ghan, Avanaddha) and give 2 examples for each. This is a highly probable question.
📌 Clearly explain the meaning of the word 'Avanaddha': 'Ava' + 'Naddha' meaning bound or covered from all sides.
📌 Mentioning Bharat Muni's 'Natyashastra' adds weight to your answer and impresses the examiner.
quick_recap: ⭐ Both Tabla and Pakhawaj fall under the 'Avanaddha Vadya' category.
⭐ Manjira, Ghunghroo, and Khartal are 'Ghan Vadya' because they are solid instruments struck together without strings or leather.
⭐ Flute (Bansuri) and Shehnai are 'Sushir Vadya' (wind instruments).
